title: Ceres Nanotrap & Dynabeads Combined Wastewater Virus Enrichment & Total Nucleic Acid Extraction
author: Victor Mabasa
materials: Select the appropriate program on the instrument (Wastewater_10mL_Virus_Isolation).

steps.title: Prepare Dynabeads enrichment plates
steps.instruction: Label and set up the following 24‑deep‑well plates: (1) Sample plate 1 with 5 000 µL clarified supernatant; (2) Dynabeads plate with 100 µL Dynabeads; (3) Sample plate 2 with 5 000 µL clarified supernatant; (4) Lysis buffer plate with 500 µL lysis buffer; (5) Tip‑comb plate (no reagent).

steps.title: Start Dynabeads enrichment run
steps.instruction: Initiate the instrument run and, when prompted, load the prepared Dynabeads sample plates, lysis buffer plate and tip‑comb plate into their designated positions.

steps.title: Prepare Ceres Nanotrap plates while Dynabeads run
steps.instruction: Label and set up the following 24‑deep‑well plates: (1) Sample plate 1 with 5 000 µL clarified supernatant; (2) Microbiome A particles plate with 75 µL particles; (3) Enhancement Reagent 1 plate with 50 µL reagent; (4) Sample plate 2 with 5 000 µL clarified supernatant; (5) Microbiome A particles plate with 75 µL particles; (6) Enhancement Reagent 1 plate with 50 µL reagent; (7) Lysis buffer plate with 500 µL lysis buffer; (8) Tip‑comb plate (no reagent).

steps.title: Complete Dynabeads enrichment and store lysis plate
steps.instruction: Approximately 20 minutes after starting the Dynabeads run, remove the lysis plate, place it at 4 °C for downstream nucleic‑acid extraction, and discard all other plates from the instrument.

steps.title: Start Ceres Nanotrap enrichment run
steps.instruction: Initiate a new instrument run and, when prompted, load the prepared Ceres Nanotrap plates (sample, particle, reagent, lysis buffer, tip‑comb) into their positions.

steps.title: Complete Ceres enrichment and store lysis plate
steps.instruction: Approximately 20 minutes after starting the Ceres Nanotrap run, remove the lysis plate, store it at 4 °C for nucleic‑acid extraction, and discard all remaining plates from the instrument.

steps.title: Prepare nucleic acid extraction binding plate while Ceres run
steps.instruction: Label and set up a 24‑deep‑well binding plate with the following contents per well: 1 000 µL combined lysed sample (to be added later), 1 040 µL binding bead mix, 80 µL Proteinase K, 1 000 µL Wash buffer 1, 1 000 µL Wash buffer 2 (80 % ethanol), 100 µL elution buffer, and a tip‑comb.

steps.title: Combine lysed material from both enrichments
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette 500 µL of lysed material from the Dynabeads lysis plate and 500 µL of lysed material from the Ceres Nanotrap lysis plate into the corresponding well of the binding plate, yielding a total of 1 000 µL lysed sample per well.

steps.title: Load binding plate and start extraction program
steps.instruction: Load the binding plate together with Wash 1, Wash 2, Elution buffer plates and a fresh tip‑comb onto the instrument. Start the run and select the program “Wastewater_10mL_Virus_Extraction”.

steps.title: Collect and store eluated nucleic acid
steps.instruction: Immediately after the run finishes, remove the Elution plate, cover it, or transfer the eluate to a new tube/plate. The nucleic acid can be used immediately or stored at –20 °C for up to 6 months, or at 80 °C for longer periods.
